classification.difficultyReason: Requires finding the altitude by Pythagoras, justifying similarity from marked right angles and the shared angle, then matching corresponding sides to derive the radius. The named triangles and ordered parts explicitly scaffold the geometric route to the circle equation.

content.prompt: A circle is inscribed in the equilateral triangle $ABC$.

spec.description: Unshaded equilateral triangle surrounding its incircle, coordinate axes through the centre, radius OX, all six printed length labels and both right-angle marks. Ordinary source blue strokes and the red centre marker use house black; the Cartesian-origin O label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=BC=6; CY=YB=3. The circle is centred at the origin, touches CB at Y and AB at X. OX is perpendicular to AB and AY is perpendicular to CB. Coordinates used internally derive the exact equilateral geometry and are not printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied geometry, labels and lengths are visible; neither the altitude nor radius is labelled with its answer.

answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras in the right-angled triangle $AYB$:
$$\begin{align*}AY^2&=AB^2-YB^2\\AY^2&=6^2-3^2\\AY^2&=27\\AY&=3\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Give reasons why $\triangle AXO$ is similar to $\triangle AYB$.

answer.short: $\angle AXO=\angle AYB=90^\circ$ and $\angle XAO=\angle YAB$; hence the triangles are similar (AA).
answer.worked: The marked right angles give $\angle AXO=\angle AYB=90^\circ$. Since $A,X,B$ are collinear and $A,O,Y$ are collinear, $\angle XAO=\angle YAB$. The remaining angles are consequently equal, so $\triangle AXO\sim\triangle AYB$ (AA, equivalently AAA).

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find $OX$ and hence find the equation of the circle.

answer.short:
$OX=\sqrt{3}$; $x^2+y^2=3$.

Use corresponding sides of the similar triangles to find the radius.
answer.worked:
Corresponding sides of $\triangle AXO$ and $\triangle AYB$ give
$$\begin{align*}\frac{OX}{YB}&=\frac{AX}{AY}\\\frac{OX}{3}&=\frac{3}{3\sqrt{3}}\\OX&=\frac{3}{\sqrt{3}}\\OX&=\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$
The circle has centre the origin and radius $OX$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+y^2&=(\sqrt{3})^2\\x^2+y^2&=3\end{align*}$$
